hypothesis: Chronological source-to-target channel transfer may deteriorate; disclosed calibration may reduce independent target-trial prediction loss. Negative findings are valid.
information_policy: Source-only tuning; chronological target75 calibration pool versus300 untouched evaluation trials. All methods use same target evaluation. Marginal normalization and target PCA receive75 unlabeled calibration trials; supervised methods receive only named prefix trial labels. Anchor methods also receive calibration commanded-target metadata. No target evaluation normalization or selection.
limitations: Two sessions of one monkey are not independent subject replicates
Channel matching does not establish stable neurons
Threshold-crossing count interpretation follows native description and integer values despite NWB volts label
No explicit quality mask; finite samples are not proof of signal quality
Native20ms clocks jitter by up to1ms; no interpolation or recomputed firing rates
Unlabeled target access differs across methods and is explicitly disclosed
Anchor alignment uses noisy commanded-target trial means, not event-time matched repeated neural responses
Moving 5-trial block interval is sensitivity analysis, not validated population uncertainty
Hyperparameters for adaptation inherited from source-only selection
No actual biological closed-loop or multisubject inference
